extracted_stakeholders.name: Penan People
extracted_stakeholders.role: Indigenous tribe living in Sarawak, Malaysia, reliant on the rainforest for their traditional lifestyle

extracted_stakeholders.name: Sarawak State Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: Government body backing commercial logging and hydroelectric dam construction on tribal lands

extracted_stakeholders.name: Survival International
extracted_stakeholders.role: Global organization campaigning for the rights and protection of tribal peoples

extracted_stakeholders.name: Shin Yang
extracted_stakeholders.role: Company involved in logging and trespassing on Penan ancestral land

extracted_factors.Label: Deforestation by Commercial Logging
extracted_factors.Description: The ongoing commercial logging in Sarawak is directly causing the destruction of the rainforest, threatening the Penan way of life and biodiversity of the region.

extracted_factors.Label: Hydroelectric Dam Construction
extracted_factors.Description: The construction of hydroelectric dams is displacing Penan communities and flooding villages, altering the landscape and impacting the Penan's traditional lifestyle.

extracted_factors.Label: Oil Palm Plantations
extracted_factors.Description: The conversion of logged forests into oil palm plantations is completely destroying forest ecosystems, making it impossible for the Penan to continue their traditional hunting and gathering lifestyle.

extracted_factors.Label: Pollution from Logging Activities
extracted_factors.Description: Pollution from logging activities is leading to river siltation and water pollution, degrading the natural resources that Penan rely on for food and water.

extracted_factors.Label: Penan Resistance and Advocacy
extracted_factors.Description: The Penan people are actively resisting the destruction of their forest through protests and advocacy, trying to protect their land and uphold their rights against external developmental pressures.
